answer: Admission is tied to one numbered heliostat bay at a desert solar tower. The applicant seats a uniquely die-stamped earth anchor through the bay's datum ring; only while the sun stands at zenith do they evaporate a measured nectar film onto a nickel coupon punched with the same stamp. Graders overlay the coupon's burn rings and pollen against that bay's official noon plate. A shared bay, a restamped rod, or a film cooked after zenith counts as one farm. Growing N aliases means leasing N bays and finishing N true-noon cooks; a copied spectrum cannot stand in.
